A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Unilaw-R1 study, with all 15 pages and Appendices A–D available. Pages 2–15 have identical extracted text and rendered content; page 1 differs only in front-matter metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Table 2, inference experiments in Tables 3 and 6, and reward-function ablations in Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, inference experiments, and reward-function ablations, including the additional experiment in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: The data-construction pipeline, SFT and GRPO training, three reward components, and Assessor–Reviser iterative inference procedure are identical in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same JEC-QA and proprietary legal-question sources and evaluate on LawBench, LexEval, and Unilaw-R1-Eval. No tasks, legal domains, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same DeepSeek, Qwen, and Unilaw model comparisons. Tables 3 and 6 retain zero-shot CoT, best-of-k, majority vote, and the same iterative-inference variants.

E3.justification: The zero-shot evaluation, metrics, dataset sizes, training configurations, and inference settings remain identical, including Table 5 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: The inference-strategy comparisons in Tables 3 and 6 and the reward-component convergence analysis in Figure 4 are unchanged. No ablations or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and convergence curves. Neither reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported trends match. Examples include Unilaw-R1's 53.2% average in Table 2 and the three-iteration average accuracies of 51.0% and 35.9% in Tables 3 and 6, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, including the GRPO objective, reward definitions, and iterative-inference updates, are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the legal datasets, two-stage training, iterative inference, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The interpretation of diminishing returns from additional inference iterations is unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning training-data coverage, text-only inputs, and insufficient evaluation of step-by-step reasoning.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D retain identical prompts, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, and inference settings. The code-access statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to previous legal reasoning and reinforcement-learning research are identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author marker and contact information for existing author Tianke Ban, revises the corresponding-author footnote, removes 'Accepted by EMNLP 2025,' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–6 retain identical content, styling, captions, and placement. Page organization is unchanged; the first-page differences are author and publication metadata edits.

improvement.justification: v2 changes corresponding-author and publication metadata while retaining the same scientific text, results, figures, limitations, and appendices. These front-matter edits establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's overall quality.
